title: Gradle: build script, tasks and incremental builds

videos.script: Lesson 1 built a small project with Maven. A pom, a lifecycle, a jar. {{maven}} This lesson builds the same two Java files with Gradle. Same sources, same dependencies, a different idea of what a build is. {{same}} Maven walks a fixed line of phases. Gradle builds a graph of tasks, and runs only the ones your request needs. {{graph}} Each task remembers what went in and what came out. Ask again with nothing changed, and Gradle does nothing at all. Change one file, and only what depends on it runs again. {{incremental}} You install Gradle once, by hand, and use it for one job: generating the wrapper. From then on the project carries its own Gradle version, and every machine builds with that one. {{wrapper}} At the end you weigh the two tools side by side. The rest of this course uses Maven, and you will know why. {{choice}}
